notes: §1985:XII.2.4 GR4: "For purposes of matching, identifier-1, word-1, and literal-1 are treated as pseudo-text containing only identifier-1, word-1, or literal-1, respectively." ReadOperand returns a non-pseudo-text operand as the text-words it spans (the word, its OF/IN qualifiers, and every parenthesized group of subscripts, arguments and reference modifier, or the one literal), ParseReplacingOperands stores those as Replacement.From exactly as it stores the words of ==pseudo-text-1==, and ApplyReplacements compares them word by word through TextWord#MatchesForReplacing, so an operand matches only whole library text words. Witness 1985-GR-XII_2_4-4 (WS-A BY WS-B leaves WS-AX: NEWBX); since kb/Work PB5469 (landed) the subscripted and reference-modified identifier and the function-identifier are read whole and matched as their pseudo-text spelling is (witness pb5469-replacing-identifier-operands). Probes p4a, p3d, p3r, p3e as before.

next.reason: 1985 GR4 treats identifier-1, word-1 and literal-1 REPLACING operands as pseudo-text for matching. The 2023 COPY format (§2023:7.2.3.2, rendered PDF p.76) has no identifier, word or literal operand, and §2023:7.2.3.4 GR8 replaces only pseudo-text-1 or partial-word-1, so no 2023 rule carries this. The stray 'word-2, or literal-4' in §2023:7.2.3.4 GR9 has no syntax behind it.
